criterionRevision: 2026-11-07, after collection: the measured outcome is the visible desktop. An owned Arena panel shows a short caption and a text box, and for about 20 seconds the same letters produce composed 你好 while open and Latin nihao while closed, switching every 5 seconds in the order open, closed, open, closed. A printed visible=True line, an IME read-back, and an empty text sample are not that measurement. No new trial was run. This remains a development trial.

limitations: The scoped desktop effect is absent from this captured trial. The mechanism stays unverified. The phase lines report set=True and mode=True, so this review does not say FinShield blocked ImmSetOpenStatus. sent=0 is the program's own foreground-window guard: it skips a key unless its window is the foreground window. The window may simply never have been foreground.

visible=True, the phase read-backs, and the empty sample are the program's own report. They are not proof the panel was on the recorded desktop. This review does not invent composed text for this trial. The five stills and the caption-bar scan show the chat only.

A runtime file-policy label in the session context is not the interception basis. This review does not name the result by that label. run.json leaves the sandbox snapshot null, and that null snapshot is not the interception basis. The pwsh call has no sandbox_permissions value. addedProtection true means owned-job recovery, the same flag the native trial records. process-recovery.json reports a Windows job object, kill-on-close, no breakaway, recovered true, and observerError null.

The caption-bar test uses the gray band of the owned panel, not character recognition of every frame. On the native baseline that band stays at or above 0.45 for 20.5 seconds. On this recording it never reaches 0.45. The five stills were also read: t36, t41, t46, and t51 fall in the job for the late recording alignment, and t56 is just after it. No still shows an Arena panel or 你好.

Two recording gaps are 0.25 seconds, at 17.125 and 31.000 seconds. The effect period is about 20 seconds. Window samples during the job are 251 to 293 milliseconds apart, and none shows the panel bounds. A flash shorter than one frame is not the measured effect.

The window list covers owned-job processes only and does not store titles. Pids 16796, 9644, and 46068 last through the job and have no enumerated window. That supports the recording. It does not identify which pid hosted the PowerShell runtime.

The native trial is a working capture baseline. It is not graded here. One decoded native frame at 45 seconds shows the panel, both scripts, and a candidate bar. This review did not read every native caption change. Decoded frames used for the scan were not added to either run.

Verified interception has no warning grade. confirmations.json is empty, approval-scope grants are empty, and no approval dialog was found. No ordinary-dialog comparison is made. The run is a development trial and is not a formal denominator entry.
